doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Basic training in Texas and the timely flu
summary: Drafted, he went to Texas basic training; flu delayed him until his transfer to California came through.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: In the draft, in those days, it was just expected, right, almost? You were going to go in the service.

Yeah, any physically able guy, I mean in a certain age limit, sure. And well I didn’t tell the whole story, but anyhow I was drafted and they sent me to Texas for Basic Training, which was out of the — whatever they call it — Vallejo is in a certain region there, whatever they call it. And Texas is a different region. And I got there and the guys are telling me you know, oh they’ll never get you because this is in a different region, they can’t do that. And I had almost given up and we were getting to the end of Basic Training. And you know you wonder how things happen — I got the flu and they put me in the hospital, so I was there a little longer than the other guys in my training unit. And I was in the hospital and one of the — what did they used to call them, the guys in the office — came up and said hey your thing came through to go to California. It’s funny I wasn’t scared or whatever, but when I think back on it, that was like, by a thread.
A timely illness at that point.

Well I’ve often wondered, like if I would have been shipped out. Well no, I had something up my sleeve. They had a good band there. It was Camp Wallace in Texas, near Houston. And the band leader there told me well gee if they don’t send for you we could use you.
They can always use a good piano player.
I guess at Texas — a little better I suppose. No Texas is great now. In those days it wasn’t considered too terrific.
